answer: Verifier nodes in a dozen regions ping every agent at random times each epoch and record round-trip latencies. The resulting profile is a mirror of where an identity really runs: fifty sybils on one rack show near-identical profiles and are folded into a single reward slot. To pass as separate agents, an attacker must host each fake in a different data center, from Lagos to a server on the tundra, paying rent for each; routing through proxies only adds hops like a tangled vine, which the timing exposes.
